subject: chemistry
title: The modern periodic table
key_idea: The modern periodic table arranges the elements in order of atomic number, so that elements with similar properties are in columns called groups. Elements in a group have the same number of outer electrons, so they react in similar ways.

blocks.text: The table is organised in rows and columns. This section covers what each one tells you.

items.meaning: A row of the periodic table. The period number is the number of shells that contain electrons.
A column of the periodic table. Elements in a group have similar properties.
The number of protons in an atom. It gives the element's position in the table.

items: The elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic (proton) number.
Elements with similar properties are placed in the same vertical column, called a group.
It is called a periodic table because similar properties occur at regular intervals.
Argon (atomic number 18) comes before potassium (19), even though potassium has the smaller relative atomic mass.
Elements are in order of atomic number, in rows called periods.
Elements with similar properties are in the same group.
The periodic table gets its name because similar properties repeat at regular intervals.

blocks.text: An element's position tells you about its electrons, and the electrons explain its chemical properties.

diagram.alt: Tap a part of the periodic table to learn what it tells you, then test yourself.

parts.name: Groups
parts.detail: The vertical columns. Elements in a group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell, which gives them similar chemical properties.

parts.name: Periods
parts.detail: The horizontal rows. The period number is the number of shells containing electrons.

parts.name: Group 1: alkali metals
parts.detail: One outer electron. They are metals that react vigorously with water.

parts.name: Group 7: halogens
parts.detail: Seven outer electrons. They are non-metals with similar reactions.

parts.name: Group 0: noble gases
parts.detail: A full outer shell. They are very unreactive.

parts.name: Transition metals
parts.detail: The block of metals between Group 2 and Group 3, such as iron and copper.

items: The group number is the number of outer-shell electrons: carbon (2,4) is in Group 4.
The period number is the number of shells: sodium (2,8,1) is in Period 3.
Elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons, so they have similar chemical properties.
Atoms react to get a full outer shell, which is more stable.
A metal atom loses its outer electrons to form a positive ion. Magnesium has 2 outer electrons, so it loses 2 to form Mg²⁺.
A non-metal atom gains electrons to form a negative ion. Chlorine has 7 outer electrons, so it gains 1 to form Cl⁻.
All halogens have 7 outer electrons, so they have similar reactions.
Group number = number of outer-shell electrons.
Period number = number of shells.
Similar outer electrons give similar chemical properties.

blocks.text: Because a group has similar chemistry, you can predict the reactions of an element from its position.

items: Nitrogen forms NH₃, so phosphorus, directly below it in the same group, forms PH₃.
Chlorine forms HCl with hydrogen, so astatine in Group 7 forms HAt.
Sodium reacts with chlorine to make NaCl, so potassium reacts with astatine to make KAt.
Moving down Group 1 the metals get more reactive. Moving down Group 7 the halogens get less reactive.
Atoms get larger down a group because they have more shells of electrons.

items.text: Tennessine has atomic number 117 and is in Group 7.
Group 7 means 7 electrons in the outer shell.
It will react like the other halogens.

items: Use the group to predict the formula of compounds and the type of reaction.
Size and reactivity change in a pattern down a group.
The number of outer electrons equals the group number.

checks.q: State how the elements are arranged in the modern periodic table.
checks.a: In order of increasing atomic number, with elements with similar properties in the same group (column).

checks.q: Explain why the elements in Group 1 have similar chemical properties.
checks.a: They all have the same number of electrons (one) in their outer shell.

checks.q: Phosphorus is directly below nitrogen in the periodic table. Predict the formula of the compound of phosphorus and hydrogen.

worked_example.question:
Very few atoms of the element tennessine (Ts) have ever been identified.

The atomic number of tennessine is 117.

Predict the number of outer shell electrons in an atom of tennessine.

Give one reason for your answer.

Use the periodic table.
answer_points: Tennessine is in Group 7 (the number of outer electrons is the same as the group number, or it is a halogen).
worked_example.tip: The reason mark depends on the correct number of electrons.

worked_example.question:
The modern periodic table is organised into groups and periods.

State in which group and in which period of the periodic table silicon is found.

You should use the periodic table to help you answer this question.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the group and one for the period. Silicon is 2,8,4: four outer electrons and three shells.

worked_example.question:
All halogens react with alkali metals to make a salt.

All halogens have similar chemical reactions.

Explain why in terms of electronic structure.
answer_points: They have the same number of electrons in the outer shell: all have 7 electrons in the outer shell.
worked_example.tip: Outer electrons or valence electrons is also accepted. The number of electrons must be correct.
